title: Wearable activity feedback after total knee replacement: a rapid review for a device lease decision
subtitle: Rapid review in eight weeks for the procurement committee of a regional orthopaedic centre
statement: The regional orthopaedic centre must decide by 10 December 2026 whether to lease 150 wrist-worn activity trackers with physiotherapist feedback for patients recovering from primary total knee replacement. The service needs a rapid review of whether wearable-based activity feedback improves physical function and activity at about three months compared with usual rehabilitation, how many patients keep using the devices, how much physiotherapist time the feedback takes, and whether older patients, people without smartphones and people living alone benefit less.
whoAffected: Adults recovering from primary total knee replacement at the centre (about 900 a year, a third aged 75 or over, many in rural areas with poor mobile coverage), the outpatient physiotherapists who would review the data, and the procurement committee that must decide on the lease.
whatHurts: Patients walk little in the first weeks after surgery and some regain function slowly. A device that adds physiotherapist workload without improving recovery, or that suits only younger patients with smartphones, would take money and clinic time away from rehabilitation that works.
currentPractice: Six weeks of group and home exercise after discharge, with physiotherapy reviews at two, six and twelve weeks and no activity monitoring between reviews.
whyNow: A supplier has offered a 12-month lease and the procurement committee meets on 10 December 2026; its chair has asked for an evidence summary before deciding.
constraints: Report due to the procurement committee on 10 December 2026, eight weeks after protocol sign-off. Searching is limited to 20 hours of information specialist time; two physiotherapists at one day a week each do screening and extraction. English-language sources only.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients regain walking and everyday function after knee replacement with rehabilitation that fits their age, home situation and access to technology.
summary: Problem framed as a rapid review for a lease decision, with function at about three months as the outcome that matters most.
